title: Communication-Efficient Robust Federated Learning with Noisy Labels

problem.claim: Federated learning must handle corrupted or noisy labels even though the server cannot easily verify the quality of locally retained data.

gap.claim: Federated bilevel optimization, particularly communication-efficient hypergradient evaluation for this setting, is under-investigated.

contributions.claim: A learning-based reweighting approach tunes a weight for each training sample using validation-set generalization performance to mitigate noisy-label effects in federated learning.
Comm-FedBiO addresses general federated bilevel optimization through two communication-efficient subroutines for hypergradient estimation.
Convergence analysis is provided for the proposed algorithms.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The approach reportedly achieves superior performance on several real-world datasets compared with various baselines.

narrative_sequence.summary: Federated learning distributes data across users and keeps it local for privacy.
Local data makes quality verification difficult, and corrupted labels harm federated learning.
The paper formulates noisy-label mitigation as federated bilevel optimization with sample reweighting based on validation generalization.
Comm-FedBiO uses two communication-efficient hypergradient-estimation subroutines and includes convergence analysis.
The proposed algorithms are applied to noisy-label learning and are reported to outperform various baselines on several real-world datasets.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the noise models, dataset names, baseline identities, or quantitative performance results.
The abstract does not provide algorithmic details, convergence conditions, communication-complexity bounds, or validation-set construction details.
